00-setup.q: Why might your commits not count toward achievements?
options: Your commit email isn't a verified email on your GitHub account
You used the command line instead of the website
00-setup.why: GitHub links commits to you by matching the author email to a verified email (or your no-reply address).

00-setup.q: What's the privacy-friendly email to use for commits?
00-setup.why: The ID+username@users.noreply.github.com address keeps your real email private and still counts.

options: In a sandbox repo you own
Only on the GitHub mobile app
00-setup.why: Practicing in your own repo means you never create noise in anyone else's project.

01-quickdraw.q: How fast do you need to close an issue or PR for Quickdraw?
01-quickdraw.why: Quickdraw is for closing an issue or pull request within five minutes of opening it.

01-quickdraw.q: An issue turns out to be a mistake. Which close reason fits?
01-quickdraw.why: "Not planned" covers won't-fix, invalid and out-of-scope reports. "Completed" means the work was done.

01-quickdraw.q: What should good triage always include?
01-quickdraw.why: A short reason keeps the project's history understandable for everyone who finds the issue later.

options: Merging a pull request without a code review
02-yolo.why: YOLO is awarded for merging a PR that nobody reviewed.
You make a branch, commit to it, push it, open a PR, then merge.

02-yolo.q: What does a branch ruleset requiring 1 approval do?
02-yolo.why: It's how teams make sure nothing reaches main unreviewed.

03-pull-shark.q: How many merged PRs earn the base Pull Shark tier?
03-pull-shark.why: The tiers are 2, 16, 128 and 1024 merged pull requests.

03-pull-shark.q: You pushed commits to your fork but never opened a PR. Do they count?
options: No, only PRs merged into the parent repo count
Only if the fork is private
03-pull-shark.why: Work that stays in your fork doesn't count until it's merged upstream.

03-pull-shark.q: Which is the honest way toward higher tiers?
options: A script that opens empty PRs
Splitting one typo fix into 20 PRs
Real fixes, docs and features in projects you use
03-pull-shark.why: Bulk or empty PRs are the spam GitHub's policies prohibit, and maintainers notice.

04-pair-extraordinaire.q: Where does the Co-authored-by trailer go?
options: At the very end of the commit message, after a blank line
04-pair-extraordinaire.why: Trailers must sit at the end of the message, separated from the body by a blank line.

04-pair-extraordinaire.q: Which email should you use for a co-author?
options: Any email you can think of
One linked to their GitHub account, like their no-reply address
04-pair-extraordinaire.why: GitHub can only credit them if the email belongs to their account.

04-pair-extraordinaire.q: Who should you list as a co-author?
options: Only people who actually contributed to that change
04-pair-extraordinaire.why: Crediting people who didn't contribute falsifies authorship.

options: Your replies being marked as the answer in Discussions
05-galaxy-brain.why: It counts accepted answers: 2, 8, 16 and 32 for the tiers.

05-galaxy-brain.q: What should a good answer lead with?
options: The fix, then why it works
A request to mark it as the answer
05-galaxy-brain.why: Busy people want the solution first. The explanation helps them learn.

05-galaxy-brain.q: Which of these breaks the rules?
options: Answering questions on GitHub's community forum
Following up to ask if it worked
Asking from one account and answering from another
05-galaxy-brain.why: Alternate accounts are fake, inauthentic interactions.

06-starstruck.q: How many stars on one repo earn the base Starstruck tier?
06-starstruck.why: The tiers are 16, 128, 512 and 4096 stars on a single repository.

06-starstruck.q: Which README element helps most in the first ten seconds?
options: A screenshot or GIF and a live demo link
06-starstruck.why: Visitors decide fast. Showing the thing working is the quickest way to earn interest.

options: They're rank abuse, which GitHub's policies prohibit
06-starstruck.why: Trading or buying stars is inauthentic activity, and accounts involved can be removed.

07-public-sponsor.why: Any sponsorship through GitHub Sponsors counts. Many maintainers accept $1.

07-public-sponsor.q: Which file adds a Sponsor button to your repo?
07-public-sponsor.why: FUNDING.yml lists where people can fund the project, and GitHub shows the button.

07-public-sponsor.q: Can't afford to sponsor? What else helps maintainers?
options: Good bug reports, docs and answering questions
07-public-sponsor.why: Time and care are real support too.

08-highlights-and-retired.q: Can you still earn Arctic Code Vault Contributor?
options: Yes, by pushing code in winter
08-highlights-and-retired.why: It was tied to the 2020 GitHub Archive Program snapshot and can't be earned anymore.

08-highlights-and-retired.q: What happens to the PRO highlight if your subscription ends?
08-highlights-and-retired.why: Highlights reflect a current status, unlike achievements.

08-highlights-and-retired.q: Someone sells a guaranteed method to get Open Sourcerer. What's true?
options: It was never released, so there's no method
08-highlights-and-retired.why: It appears in GitHub's assets but was never released.

git-01-how-git-works.q: What is a branch in Git?
options: A full copy of your code
A movable label pointing at one commit
git-01-how-git-works.why: That's why creating a branch is instant, even in huge projects.

options: Which branch or commit you're on right now
git-01-how-git-works.why: HEAD is "you are here". New commits move whichever branch HEAD points at.

git-01-how-git-works.q: Which command moves changes into the staging area?
git-01-how-git-works.why: git add stages changes. git commit saves what's staged into history.

git-02-everyday-loop.q: Which shows exactly what will go into your next commit?
git-02-everyday-loop.why: Plain git diff shows unstaged changes. --staged shows what's queued for the commit.

git-02-everyday-loop.q: Which is the best commit subject?
options: Fix crash when the cart is empty
Fixes: various bugs in many files.
git-02-everyday-loop.why: Short, imperative, and specific about what the commit does.

git-02-everyday-loop.q: What does git add -p let you do?
git-02-everyday-loop.why: Interactive staging builds focused commits and catches stray debug lines.

git-03-branching-and-merging.q: When does a fast-forward merge happen?
options: When both branches have new commits
When the target branch hasn't moved since you branched
git-03-branching-and-merging.why: Git just slides the label forward, so no merge commit is needed.

git-03-branching-and-merging.q: In a conflict, what's between <<<<<<< HEAD and =======?
git-03-branching-and-merging.why: The top half is yours (HEAD). The bottom half, before >>>>>>>, is incoming.

git-03-branching-and-merging.q: How do you back out of a merge in progress?
git-03-branching-and-merging.why: It puts everything back exactly as it was before the merge.

git-04-rebase.q: What does rebase do to your commits?
options: Replays them on a new base as new commits with new IDs
git-04-rebase.why: Same changes, new parents, so new IDs. That's why the golden rule exists.

git-04-rebase.q: What's the golden rule of rebasing?
options: Never rebase commits others have already based work on
git-04-rebase.why: Rewriting shared history breaks your teammates' copies.

git-04-rebase.q: After rebasing your own PR branch, how should you push?
git-04-rebase.why: --force-with-lease refuses to overwrite commits you haven't seen.

git-05-remotes.q: What's the difference between fetch and pull?
options: Fetch downloads without changing your files. Pull also merges or rebases
git-05-remotes.why: Fetch is always safe. Pull updates your current branch too.

git-05-remotes.q: Your push is rejected because GitHub has commits you don't. What do you do?
git-05-remotes.why: Bring their commits down first. Forcing would throw them away.

git-05-remotes.q: What does git push -u origin my-feature do?
options: Pushes and links your branch to origin/my-feature
git-05-remotes.why: After that, plain git push and git pull know where to go.

git-06-power-tools.q: Which command finds the commit that introduced a bug, using binary search?
git-06-power-tools.why: Bisect halves the range each step, so 80 commits take about 7 tests.

git-06-power-tools.q: You committed .env before adding it to .gitignore. What's still true?
options: Ignoring it removes it from history
The secret is still in your history
git-06-power-tools.why: Stop tracking it with git rm --cached, and rotate the secret.

git-06-power-tools.q: How do you copy one commit from another branch onto yours?
git-06-power-tools.why: Cherry-pick applies that single commit's changes as a new commit.

github-01-profile.q: What's the repo name for a profile README?
github-01-profile.why: A public repo named exactly like your username shows its README on your profile.

github-01-profile.q: How many repos can you pin to your profile?
github-01-profile.why: Up to six repositories or gists.

github-01-profile.q: What does the contribution graph measure?
github-01-profile.why: It shows activity, not skill. Nobody serious judges you by green squares.

github-02-issues-and-projects.q: What does "Fixes #42" in a PR description do when the PR merges into the default branch?
github-02-issues-and-projects.why: Closing keywords link the PR and issue, and close the issue on merge.

github-02-issues-and-projects.q: Which labels does GitHub use to suggest your issues to newcomers?
options: good first issue and help wanted
github-02-issues-and-projects.why: These two labels are special and surface your issues to new contributors.

github-02-issues-and-projects.q: What do sub-issues let you do?
options: Break a big issue into smaller tracked ones
github-02-issues-and-projects.why: The parent shows progress as its sub-issues close.

github-03-code-review.q: Which PR is easiest to review well?
options: A small, focused PR with a clear description
A PR that fixes three unrelated things
github-03-code-review.why: Small, focused PRs get faster and more thorough reviews.

github-03-code-review.q: How do you propose an exact code change a reviewer can apply in one click?
options: A suggestion block in a review comment
github-03-code-review.why: A ```suggestion block shows an Apply button to the author.

github-03-code-review.q: What does a CODEOWNERS file do?
options: Requests reviews from the right people automatically
github-03-code-review.why: Matching paths automatically request reviews from their owners.

github-04-actions.why: GitHub only runs YAML files in .github/workflows/.

github-04-actions.q: Where should an API key used by a workflow go?
options: In Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
github-04-actions.why: Secrets are encrypted and masked in logs. Never put them in the YAML.

github-04-actions.q: Why pass an issue title through env: instead of writing it straight into run:?
options: The title could contain shell commands that would run
github-04-actions.why: Untrusted text placed directly into a script is a classic injection risk.

github-05-releases.q: You add a new feature without breaking anything. 2.4.1 becomes…
github-05-releases.why: New compatible features bump MINOR and reset PATCH.

options: Merged PRs and new contributors since the last release
github-05-releases.why: Add a human-written highlights section on top.

github-05-releases.q: What must good release notes always call out?
options: Breaking changes and how to upgrade
github-05-releases.why: Users need to know what might break for them.

github-06-security.why: Passkeys and security keys resist phishing. SMS can be intercepted.

options: Blocks pushes that contain known secret formats
github-06-security.why: It stops a leaked key before it ever reaches GitHub.

github-06-security.q: A token was leaked. What's the FIRST thing to do?
github-06-security.why: Assume it's already been copied. Deleting the commit doesn't un-leak it.

github-07-open-source.q: Before working on a bigger change, what should you do?
options: Open a huge PR right away
Comment on the issue with your plan and wait for agreement
github-07-open-source.why: This one step prevents most rejected PRs.

github-07-open-source.q: No reply to your PR after a week. What's reasonable?
options: Be patient, and nudge politely after about two weeks
github-07-open-source.why: Many maintainers are volunteers. A week of silence is normal.

options: Unread AI-generated PRs sent to many repos
github-07-open-source.why: Unreviewed automated PRs burn out maintainers.
